strategy.summary: Reproduce GH-60303 in pandas: group_sum in pandas/_libs/groupby.pyx accumulates float sums with Kahan compensation; when the running sum overflows to +/-inf, the compensation term becomes NaN and the group result is NaN instead of +/-inf. The developer's test test_cython_group_sum_overflow in pandas/tests/groupby/test_libgroupby.py calls group_sum directly with three copies of np.finfo(np.float64).max (and complex variants) and expects inf; it should fail on the buggy commit a7e0900cfb75 and pass on the fixed revision.
strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/groupby/test_libgroupby.py::test_cython_group_sum_overflow (parametrized over 8 value cases: float64 max/min and complex128 combinations, GH-60303)
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision a7e0900cfb75 the parametrized test fails: group_sum writes NaN into the float64 case where inf is expected (and NaN components in complex cases), so tm.assert_numpy_array_equal reports a mismatch. On the fixed revision (the PR that adds isfinite checks on the compensation term and resets it to 0 when non-finite) all 8 parametrized cases pass.
strategy.numerical_probe: Call group_sum(actual, counts, data, labels, None, is_datetimelike=False) with data = np.array([[np.finfo(np.float64).max] for _ in range(3)]) and labels np.array([0,0,0], dtype=np.intp); inspect actual[0,0] is inf on fixed, NaN on buggy.
risks: Only the compiled Cython extension reflects the fix; the editable build must be rebuilt after switching between buggy and fixed revisions, otherwise the test result is stale.

Reproduction is documented only by an issue report on Windows with Python 3.11.9 and an older commit 0691c5cf90477d3503834d983f69350f250a6ff7; the failure is arithmetic and should be platform-independent on IEEE-754 float64, but this was not confirmed on Linux here.
pytest and hypothesis versions are undocumented and unbounded; pick current releases compatible with the pandas revision's test suite.
NumPy version is unbounded in the evidence; choose a version compatible with the buggy commit's Cython build, and note that the test relies on np.complex128 construction behaviour.

Compiler and optimisation flags could in principle affect whether the intermediate inf propagates into the compensation term (e.g. fast-math); the default build should preserve IEEE semantics, but this is an assumption.
The test imports group_sum from pandas._libs.groupby; ensure the test module import path resolves to the built extension in the editable install.

oracle.reference_source: developer test expected values (inf, -inf, complex infinities) via tm.assert_numpy_array_equal
oracle.why: The expected results are exact IEEE infinities from overflow of finite inputs, so exact comparison is appropriate; no tolerance is needed.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On buggy a7e0900cfb75 group_sum yields NaN for the float64 max case where inf is asserted; assert_numpy_array_equal sees NaN != inf and the test fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the isfinite guard resets compensation to 0 when the sum overflows, so the result is inf (or -inf / the expected complex components) and the assertion holds.
